chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about a man who stands in salat (prayer) and forgets Fatihat al-Kitab. He said:
Then let him say: “I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.”
Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

Then let him recite it so long as he has not yet bowed, for there is no salat (prayer) for him until he recites it, whether aloud or quietly. But if he has bowed, that will suffice for him, if Allah wills.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it sufficed him, meaning the prayer counts as valid
key_terms.أَسْتَعِيذُ: I seek refuge, an invocation of protection before recitation
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ: the accursed Satan, from whom refuge is sought
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Fatihat al-Kitab, the opening surah required in recitation

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets Fatihat al-Kitab during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who forgets to recite Fatihat al-Kitab in salat (prayer). If he remembers before ruku', he must recite it; if he has already bowed, the prayer is deemed sufficient, if Allah wills.
